title: What is a tri-merge credit report? A guide for lenders
summary: A tri-merge credit report merges Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion data into one deduplicated report with a score from each bureau, and mortgage lenders use the middle score. This guide covers how it is built, how the representative score works, and where tri-merge policy stands as of October 14, 2026.
body_markdown:
A tri-merge credit report combines a borrower's Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion credit reports into one merged report, with duplicate data removed. It also carries a credit score from each of the three bureaus. Mortgage lenders typically use the middle of those three scores as the borrower's qualifying score, per[Fannie Mae's Selling Guide](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.1-02/determining-credit-score-mortgage-loan) .


For credit product, risk, and underwriting teams, the tri-merge is also a moving policy target. FHFA has added VantageScore 4.0, FHA has kept the tri-merge, and a bi-merge option is reportedly under consideration.


This guide explains how a tri-merge credit report is built, what it contains, and how the representative score works. It also covers policy status as of October 14, 2026, and how to order one correctly.


### How a tri-merge credit report is built


A tri-merge starts as three separate bureau files and ends as one lender-ready document. A credit reporting vendor performs the merge before the lender receives the report.


[Fannie Mae's Selling Guide](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.2-02/types-credit-reports) describes an automated merged report as one that "combines the in-file credit reports from multiple repositories into a single report." For loans run through Desktop Underwriter, lenders must order the three-file merged report from a credit information provider[listed by Fannie Mae](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.2-01/requirements-credit-reports) .


During the merge, the vendor may delete duplicate information, translate codes into plain language, and resolve conflicting data, according to[Fannie Mae](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.2-01/requirements-credit-reports) . It may not delete legitimate negative items, such as tradelines tied to a borrower's bankruptcy.


There is no single industry-standard deduplication method.[Freddie Mac's guide](https://guide.freddiemac.com/app/guide/section/5203.1) notes that "each CRC may use a slightly different merge logic to eliminate duplicate records." Fannie Mae also notes that public records[may appear in the report three times](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-2-09/erroneous-credit-report-data) , one per bureau, and that DU ignores duplicate accounts it identifies.


‍


### What's in a tri-merge credit report


The contents follow GSE minimum standards, so most mortgage tri-merge reports share the same core sections. Individual vendor formats vary.


- Identifying information, such as name, date of birth, addresses, and co-applicant names, per the[CFPB](https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_consumer-reporting-companies_list_2025.pdf) .
- Tradelines with creditor name, open date, highest credit, status, required payment, unpaid balance, and payment history, per[Fannie Mae](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.2-01/requirements-credit-reports) .
- Public records, principally bankruptcies, per the[CFPB's 2025 consumer reporting companies list](https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_consumer-reporting-companies_list_2025.pdf) .
- Every inquiry made in the previous 90 days, which[Fannie Mae requires](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.2-01/requirements-credit-reports) the report to list.
- A credit score from each of the three bureaus, requested for each borrower when the report is ordered, per[Fannie Mae](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.1-01/general-requirements-credit-scores) .


[Fannie Mae requires](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.2-01/requirements-credit-reports) the report to include "both credit and public record information for each borrower." Judgments or liens appear only where they are found and reported.


‍


### How the middle score works on a tri-merge credit report


The representative credit score drives mortgage pricing, so getting the logic right matters.[Fannie Mae's rule](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.1-02/determining-credit-score-mortgage-loan) works in two steps.


#### One borrower


When three scores are available, the lender uses the middle score. When only two are available, the lender uses the lower one.


Two-bureau files are acceptable only in narrow cases. Examples include a borrower with data at only two bureaus, or a credit freeze at one bureau, per[Fannie Mae](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.2-02/types-credit-reports) .


#### Multiple borrowers


The lender first finds each borrower's middle (or lower) score. It then selects the lowest of those scores as the loan's representative credit score.


Consider a hypothetical loan. Borrower A scores 702, 715, and 731, so A's score is 715. Borrower B scores 688, 694, and 740, so B's score is 694, and the loan's representative score is 694.


That lowest score is used for pricing on all loans. For certain manually underwritten transactions, though, the average median credit score is used for eligibility, per[Selling Guide B3-5.1-02](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.1-02/determining-credit-score-mortgage-loan) . If the example above fell under that rule, the eligibility score would be 704.5.


The[Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac Partner Playbook (September 2026)](https://singlefamily.fanniemae.com/media/34286/display) confirms that the same representative score logic applies to VantageScore 4.0.


‍


### Single-pull vs. bi-merge vs. tri-merge


The three formats differ only in how many bureaus feed the report. The[Consumer Data Industry Association (CDIA)](https://www.cdiaonline.org/cdia-statements/2025/10/20/tri-merge-credit-reporting-is-essential-for-lenders-and-borrowers/) defines them this way.


- A single-pull report relies on data from one bureau.
- A bi-merge report combines information from two bureaus.
- A tri-merge report consolidates data from all three bureaus.


The[FHFA Office of Inspector General](https://www.fhfaoig.gov/sites/default/files/AUD-2025-008.pdf) notes that lenders have historically delivered a tri-merge report with reports and scores from all three bureaus.


### Tri-merge policy status as of October 14, 2026


As of October 14, 2026, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and FHA all still require tri-merge reports. The scoring models are changing faster than the report format.


#### FHFA, Fannie Mae, and Freddie Mac


According to the[FHFA credit scores page](https://www.fhfa.gov/policy/credit-scores) (last updated October 2, 2026), lenders can choose Classic FICO or VantageScore 4.0. They must use the same model for all borrowers on a loan.


- VantageScore 4.0 became available to all approved lenders on September 9, 2026.
- FHFA aligned fees across Classic FICO and VantageScore 4.0 on September 30, 2026.
- FICO 10T is approved but "not currently eligible for delivery."
- Classic FICO is expected to retire at a future date, but FHFA has announced no retirement date.


FHFA states that adding VantageScore 4.0 will not change the Enterprises' current credit reporting requirements.


#### FHA


HUD[states](https://www.hud.gov/hud-partners/single-family-fha-info) that FHA "will continue to require the use of a tri-merge credit report." HUD has also set a January 1, 2027 start for new score models.


For FHA case numbers assigned on or after that date, lenders may submit VantageScore 4.0 and FICO Score 10T alongside Classic FICO, per[HUD](https://www.hud.gov/hud-partners/single-family-fha-info) . This applies to Title II forward mortgages.


#### The bi-merge debate


Bi-merge has a long history at FHFA. Per the[FHFA credit scores page](https://www.fhfa.gov/policy/credit-scores) , FHFA first announced a bi-merge option in October 2022. In January 2025, it moved implementation to a date to be determined, and a July 2025 interim policy kept the tri-merge.


In October 2026, FHFA was reportedly preparing to allow bi-merge again.[HousingWire, citing Bloomberg](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/fhfa-bi-merge-credit-reports-fannie-freddie/) , reported the change could come within weeks and take effect one to three months after announcement.


FHFA Director Bill Pulte said in a post on X that FHFA was "seriously considering bi-merge,"[HousingWire reported](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/fhfa-bi-merge-credit-report-vantagescore-pulte/) on September 4, 2026. He then[canceled an in-person MBA Annual appearance](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/mba-tri-merge-credit-report/) where many expected an announcement. As of October 14, 2026, the sources reviewed for this article show no formal bi-merge directive.


‍


### Who can order a tri-merge credit report


A tri-merge is a consumer report, so the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) controls who can get one. Section 604 lets a bureau furnish a consumer report only in listed circumstances "and no other," per[15 U.S.C. §1681b](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1681b) .


A lender needs a permissible purpose, such as a credit transaction involving the consumer, under[FCRA Section 604(a)(3)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1681b) . Under[FCRA Section 607(a)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1681e) (15 U.S.C. §1681e), users must identify themselves and certify the purpose of the report. The agency may not furnish a report when it has reasonable grounds to believe it won't be used for a permissible purpose.


‍


### Tri-merge credit reports and hard inquiries


A lender's pull for a credit application is a hard inquiry. The[CFPB's 2025 list](https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_consumer-reporting-companies_list_2025.pdf) explains that soft inquiries are not shared with third parties and do not affect scores.


Scoring models limit the impact of mortgage rate shopping. Recent FICO versions count multiple mortgage inquiries within 45 days as a single inquiry, per[myFICO](https://www.myfico.com/credit-education/credit-reports/manage-credit-inquiries) . The same page notes that FICO Scores only consider inquiries from the last 12 months.


‍


### The tri-merge cost debate


Every cost figure in this debate comes from an interested party. We found no neutral, authoritative price for a tri-merge report.


- The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) estimates costs will rise "by another 40% to 50%" in 2026, per[Scotsman Guide](https://www.scotsmanguide.com/news/mba-urges-fhfa-to-drop-tri-merge-credit-score-mandate/) .
- The MBA supports a single report when the initial report shows a credit score of 700 or above, per[Scotsman Guide](https://www.scotsmanguide.com/news/mba-urges-fhfa-to-drop-tri-merge-credit-score-mandate/) .
- The Community Home Lenders of America (CHLA) warns that single-pull reporting could increase repurchase risk, per[CHLA's January 14, 2026 paper](https://www.communitylender.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/CHLA-Addendume-Single-Bureau-Credit-Pull-Model.pdf) .
- CHLA's member survey puts per-loan credit report costs at about $50 in 2022 and roughly $540 in 2026, per[HousingWire](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/fico-tri-merge-price-jump/) .
- [FICO lists](https://investors.fico.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fico-launches-cost-cutting-direct-license-program-mortgage) $4.95 per score plus a $33 funded-loan fee per borrower per score under its performance model, or $10 per score via resellers.
- [FICO says](https://investors.fico.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fico-launches-cost-cutting-direct-license-program-mortgage) it does not control the markups bureaus and resellers add to those fees.
- Equifax will keep $1 VantageScore 4.0 mortgage score pricing through 2028,[HousingWire reported](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/mortgage-score-costs/) on October 9, 2026.
- TransUnion will keep 99-cent VantageScore 4.0 pricing through 2028 when pulled alongside a FICO score, per the same[HousingWire report](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/mortgage-score-costs/) .


CHLA's $540 figure covers total credit-report-related costs on a conventional loan. It is not the price of the report itself. The Equifax and TransUnion figures are score prices, not report prices.


‍


### Where tri-merge fits outside mortgage lending


The tri-merge is a GSE and FHA mortgage convention. Non-mortgage and business lenders choose their own data mix.


SBA's revised 7(a) Small underwriting allows scoring models that do "not rely solely on consumer credit scores," per[NAGGL](https://www.naggl.org/sba-notice-formally-announcing-sunsetting-of-sbss-scoring-and-providing-new-underwriting-requirements-for-7a-small-loans/) . For business lending teams,[Lendflow Connect](https://www.lendflow.com/lendflow-connect) aggregates credit bureau and business data, and[Lendflow Intelligence](https://www.lendflow.com/lendflow-intelligence) turns it into lending decisions.


‍


### How to order and use a tri-merge credit report


Use this six-step process to keep mortgage credit pulls compliant and pricing accurate.


1. Document the FCRA permissible purpose for each borrower, and complete your provider's purpose certification.
2. Order through an approved provider, such as a credit information provider on Fannie Mae's list for DU loans.
3. Choose Classic FICO or VantageScore 4.0, and apply that model to every borrower on the loan.
4. Review the merged file for repeated public records, retained negative items, and any bureau with a freeze or thin file.
5. Calculate the representative score using each borrower's middle (or lower) score, then the lowest across borrowers for pricing.
6. For manually underwritten multi-borrower loans, confirm whether the average median credit score applies to eligibility.


‍


### Best practices for tri-merge credit report workflows


Policy shifts and score logic shortcuts create avoidable tri-merge errors. These practices help teams stay accurate.


- Recheck the FHFA credit scores page and GSE lender letters before every policy change, since bi-merge status could shift quickly.
- Expect merge logic to differ by vendor, and test sample files when switching providers.
- Separate pricing logic from eligibility logic in your loan origination system for multi-borrower loans.
- Treat cost claims from CDIA, MBA, CHLA, and FICO as positions, and budget against your own vendor invoices.
- Avoid telling borrowers that Classic FICO is retired or that FICO 10T is live, since neither is true as of October 14, 2026.


A common pitfall is assuming the lowest borrower score drives every decision. It drives pricing, but certain manually underwritten loans use the average median score for eligibility.


#### Key takeaways on tri-merge credit reports


A tri-merge credit report merges Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion data into one deduplicated report with a score from each bureau. Mortgage lenders use the middle score per borrower and the lowest of those across borrowers for pricing.


As of October 14, 2026, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and FHA still require it. FHFA is reportedly weighing bi-merge, so build credit workflows that can absorb a format change without rework.


‍


### Frequently asked questions about tri-merge credit reports


#### Is a tri-merge credit report a hard inquiry?


Yes. A lender's pull for a credit application is a hard inquiry, per the CFPB. Recent FICO versions count multiple mortgage inquiries within 45 days as one.


#### Which score do lenders use from a tri-merge credit report?


Fannie Mae lenders use the middle of three scores, or the lower of two. With multiple borrowers, the lowest of those scores becomes the loan's representative score.


#### What happens if a borrower's three scores differ widely?


Under[Fannie Mae's middle-score rule](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-5.1-02/determining-credit-score-mortgage-loan) , the middle score still applies. As a result, one unusually high or low score does not set the qualifying score. Lenders should review the underlying tradelines to understand the gap.


#### How much does a tri-merge credit report cost?


No single authoritative price exists. MBA, CHLA, and FICO publish conflicting figures, so lenders should rely on their own provider pricing.


#### Has FHFA switched to bi-merge?


Not as of October 14, 2026, based on the sources reviewed. FHFA is reportedly preparing a bi-merge option, but no formal directive had been published.
